newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Regrade widens on weak gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Regrade widens on weak gas oil.

text.p: The Singapore jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade widened at midday on Thursday amid weak gas oil prices and steady demand for jet fuel, traders said.
"The regrade widened after the gas oil market was thrashed because of the prompt overhang," one trader said.
The July and August regrade was last quoted at $1.00/$1.30 per barrel with the bids seen able to improve further, brokers said.
July regrade last traded at 75 cents early this week, they said.
Traders said the regrade widened partly because of the large falls to gas oil prices where July fell to around $21.50 on Wednesday from over $23.00 per barrel last week.

The differing strength of the two markets was clearly seen in the physical markets where on Wednesday jet fuel traded at $23.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for Jul 3-7 lifting compared to a gas oil trade at $21.45 per barrel also for July 3-7 lifting.

In addition to the weak gas oil market, the regrade was also boosted by firmer jet fuel values due to steady regional demand where Indonesia raised its July purchases to around two million barrels, up about 500,000 barrels from its usual monthly purchases.

However, traders said the firmer jet fuel prices may be shortlived. This is because refiners have so far not switched operations to optimise jet fuel production but might be encouraged to do so in the wake of higher jet prices, which might in turn lead to higher stocks and lower prices.
"I think the refiners will switch to maximise jet fuel production soon because the regrades are looking very attractive," one trader said.
Gas oil swaps rebounded from its overnight lows as the market corrected the recent sharp falls.
July paper was last quoted at $21.80/$22.00 per barrel, up from late Wednesday's $21.50/$21.70, brokers said.
August swaps also firmed, keeping the July/August spread steady at minus 60 cents, they said. August was last quoted up about 30 cents from Wednesday at $22.55/$22.70.
Fuel oil swaps fell in line with the crude market with July last quoted at $98.75/$99.50 from $99.25/$99.75, brokers said.
Overnight August Brent crude closed down 31 cents to $17.77 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
